result.title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are becoming direct users of the open web. As they take on increasingly complex and information-intensive tasks, effective web access is becoming a core capability for agentic problem solving. Existing approaches have advanced agentic web access through different access models, including search-augmented agents, browser-based agents, and, more recently, filesystem-based agents. Nevertheless, as users expect agents to complete long-horizon, end-to-end tasks, they increasingly need to conduct broad information gathering, perform browser actions, and revisit acquired evidence within a single trajectory. Yet our preliminary analyses reveal that existing access models struggle to meet these demands. They primarily support either information gathering or browser interaction, while combining their capabilities can involve substantial costs or performance trade-offs. To this end, we present Web\$hell, an interface that unifies web access under a single access model. Using a common schema defined by WebContract, WebCompiler compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects. These objects are maintained in WebCache and handled through a shared set of operations, providing agents with consistent, operable, and persistent web access. Through extensive experiments across web search, web navigation, and deep research benchmarks, we show that Web\$hell achieves strong task performance at lower cost. Our results further indicate the importance of interface design for effective web access, with Web\$hell opening new possibilities for more capable and efficient LLM agents on the web.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Web$hell：用 WebContract 定义统一 schema，由 WebCompiler 把实时网页编译为可寻址的信息与动作对象，存在 WebCache 中由共享操作处理，并在搜索、导航与深度研究基准上以更低成本取得较好表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理主线无关，但其「把环境状态编译为可寻址对象并持久缓存、供轨迹内复用证据」的设计可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据寻址、复现与 LOOK/STOP 决策提供类比线索，需较多核查。
